input.model_so_far: Frame with fork-J (shift housing, carrying knob-I) hanging in the middle, bracket-G and bracket-H either side.

new_parts.name: bush-K
new_parts.position: near the left end of axle-N, against the frame

new_parts.name: gear-gray-L
new_parts.catalog_name: Technic Gear 16 Tooth with Round Holes
new_parts.position: on axle-N, just right of bush-K

new_parts.name: gear-tan-M
new_parts.catalog_name: Technic Gear 20 Tooth Double Bevel with Axle Hole Type 2
new_parts.position: on axle-N, near the right end, inside fork-R

new_parts.name: axle-N
new_parts.position: the main gear shaft, running the length of the frame through bush-K, gear-gray-L and gear-tan-M, and out through fork-R's bearing hole on the right

what_each_new_part_touches: axle-N's 1st cross point locks into bush-K's cross hole
axle-N's 3rd cross point locks into gear-gray-L's cross hole
axle-N's 7th cross point locks into gear-tan-M's cross hole
axle-N's far end turns freely in fork-R's round hole~
where_everything_is_after: axle-N: new main shaft, running the length of the frame
bush-K, gear-gray-L, gear-tan-M: fixed to axle-N, turning with it
fork-R: now holding the shaft's right-hand bearing

why.problem_solved: Builds the main gear shaft that will carry the clutch mechanism and drive the output.
why.why_these_parts: gear-gray-L and gear-tan-M are locked to the shaft (cross-hole gears) so they always turn with it; bush-K keeps the shaft from sliding left; fork-R's round hole lets the shaft spin free on the right.
why.sets_up_for_later: gear-gray-L will mesh with the input gear added in step 10. The dog-clutch sleeve (step 9) and the second clutch gear (step 8) go on this same shaft, between gear-gray-L and gear-tan-M. The shaft's right end takes an output extension in step 11.

review_note: Exactly which numbered cross-point of axle-N each part sits at isn't shown with hole markers -- read left to right in the order bush-K, gear-gray-L, (gap for steps 8-9's clutch), gear-tan-M, matching their left-to-right order in the picture, with axle-N's far tip sitting in fork-R's hole (marked ~, estimated). gear-gray-L and gear-tan-M are locked (cross-hole) parts in the catalog, so they always turn with the shaft; whether that's mechanically correct for how the gearbox actually shifts speed is an open question -- see systems.json.
